newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian businessman files lawsuit over Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian businessman files lawsuit over Busang.

text.p: Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh said on Wednesday he had filed a C$2 billion lawsuit ($1.48 billion) in Canada against Bre-X Minerals Ltd on their ownership dispute over the Busang gold find in Kalimantan.
"Yes, I can confirm that I filed the suit yesterday and its for C$2 billion," he told Reuters.
He said the legal action was taken to reinforce his claim to the Busang gold deposit, but added that he would withdraw the suit if Bre-X agreed to his ownership claim.
"So far there's been no response from Bre-X," he said. "But if Bre-X agrees to my claim, I will withdraw my suit. They have to come to the negotiating table."
Warren Beckwith, managing director of Golden Valley Mines NL which has a technical and financial deal with Merukh's PT Krueng Gasui, said Merukh filed the suit in Calgary.
Merukh had said he owned 40 percent of the entire Busang property, which was not recognised by Bre-X, and demanded Bre-X begin negotiations to resolve the ownership dispute.

The Canadian Press news agency said Merukh and two companies he is associated with, PT Krueng Gasui and PT Sungai Atan Perdana, said they were left out of the exploration programme that led to the discovery of the Southeast Busang gold find.
Merukh's companies were each left holding a 10 percent interest in the much smaller Busang Central deposit.

The lawsuit was filed in the Court of Queen's Bench of Alberta by PT Krueng Gasui, which is claiming a 10 percent interest in the Southeast Busang find along with an option on an additional 20 percent, the agency reported.
The suit named Bre-X chief executive David Walsh and senior vice-president John Felderhof, the Canadian Press said.
Also named are Indonesian Syakerani and his son Ahmad Yani, the agency said. Their family controls PT Askatindo Karya Mineral, which owns a 10 percent interest in the motherlode.
"We don't know anything about that," said Bre-X spokesman Steve McAnulty, when contacted in Calgary by Reuters.
McAnulty said his company had not been in contact with Merukh for weeks if not months. Walsh told Reuters in an earlier interview on Tuesday that Merukh's claims had no merit.

The suit arises out of a 1987 joint venture known as PT Westralian Atan Minerals, consisting of Merukh's two firms, each with a 10 percent interest, and an Australian company, Westralian Resource Projects Ltd, with an 80 percent interest.
Golden Valley told Reuters the suit said there was a failure of fiduciary obligations to act in the best interests of Merukh and his firms and alleges misuse of confidential information.
Bre-X estimates the property contains at least 57 million ounces of gold worth over $21 billion at current prices.
In another twist to the Busang saga, Syakerani told Reuters on Wednesday he had sold a stake in his company PT Askatindo to local timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hasan.
"I sold it for national interest. I am very happy with the deal, and my position in the company is still good," he said.
He said Hasan would inject funds into Askatindo, which has a 10 percent stake in the richest parts of the Busang find.

Syakareni said Hasan had been made president-commissioner and Harsono, the president-director of PT Panutan Duta, had been named president-director in a management reshuffle. Panutan is controlled by President Suharto's eldest son Sigit Hardojudanto.

Meanwhile, Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc on Tuesday offered a "merger-of-equals" with Bre-X, which Placer chief executive John Willson said would allow Bre-X to end up with 45 to 55 percent of the combined company.
He pegged the deal's worth at C$6.75 billion ($5 billion), or roughly half the value of the combined companies.

Bre-X and Canada's Barrick Gold Corp have made a joint submission to Indonesia's Mines and Energy Ministry outlining their agreement to jointly develop the property, but the ministry has yet to respond.
